questions.q: What is the main function of the sepal in a flower?
questions.explain: The sepal protects the flower while it is still a bud.
procedure: The sepal is the green, leaf-like part at the base of the flower
While the flower is still a bud, the sepal wraps around it
This protects the delicate inner parts from damage and weather
Once the flower opens, the sepal stays at the base
Answer: To protect the flower bud

questions.q: What is the coloured part of a flower called?
questions.explain: Petals are the bright, coloured parts of a flower.
procedure: Look at any flower — the colourful leaves you see are petals
Petals are usually bright and attractive
Their colour and scent attract insects and birds
Answer: Petal

questions.q: Which part of a flower produces pollen?
questions.explain: The stamen is the male part of the flower and produces pollen.
procedure: The stamen is the male part of the flower
It has two parts: the anther and the filament
The anther at the top produces the yellow pollen grains
Answer: Stamen

questions.q: Which part of the flower receives pollen during pollination?
questions.explain: The stigma is the top of the pistil and receives pollen grains.
procedure: The pistil is the female part of the flower
Its top is called the stigma
The stigma is sticky, so pollen grains stick to it
Answer: Stigma

questions.q: What is the male part of a flower called?
questions.explain: The stamen is the male part of a flower.
procedure: Flowers have both male and female parts
The male part is called the stamen
It produces pollen, which contains the male sex cells
Answer: Stamen

questions.q: What is the female part of a flower called?
questions.explain: The pistil is the female part of a flower.
procedure: The female part of a flower is the pistil
It has three parts: stigma, style, and ovary
The ovary contains the egg cells (ovules)
Answer: Pistil

questions.q: Which part of the pistil contains the egg cells?
questions.explain: The ovary is at the base of the pistil and contains the egg cells.
procedure: The pistil has three parts: stigma (top), style (middle), and ovary (bottom)
The ovary is the swollen base of the pistil
Inside the ovary are the ovules (egg cells)
After fertilization, the ovary becomes the fruit
Answer: Ovary

questions.q: What is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma called?
questions.explain: Pollination is the transfer of pollen to the stigma.
procedure: Pollination = movement of pollen from anther to stigma
It can happen within the same flower or between flowers
Wind, insects, birds, and water can carry pollen
Answer: Pollination

questions.q: After pollination, what happens to the pollen grain on the stigma?
options: It grows a tube down to the ovary
questions.answer: It grows a tube down to the ovary
questions.explain: The pollen grain grows a pollen tube down through the style to reach the ovary.
procedure: A pollen grain lands on the sticky stigma
It grows a long tube called the pollen tube
The tube grows down through the style to the ovary
The male sex cell travels down the tube to join the egg cell
Answer: It grows a tube down to the ovary

questions.q: What is formed when the male and female sex cells join?
questions.explain: The joining of male and female cells forms a seed.
procedure: Fertilization = when male and female cells join
The fertilized egg cell develops into a seed
The ovary around it becomes the fruit
Answer: A seed

questions.q: Which part of the flower becomes the fruit after fertilization?
questions.explain: After fertilization, the ovary grows into the fruit.
procedure: Before fertilization: the ovary holds the ovules (egg cells)
After fertilization: the ovules become seeds
The ovary itself grows and becomes the fruit
This is why every fruit contains seeds
Answer: The ovary

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a part of the stamen?
questions.explain: The stigma is part of the pistil, not the stamen.
procedure: Stamen = anther + filament (male parts)
Pistil = stigma + style + ovary (female parts)
The stigma belongs to the pistil, not the stamen
Answer: Stigma

questions.q: What is the stalk that supports the anther called?
questions.explain: The filament is the thin stalk that holds up the anther.
procedure: The stamen has two parts: anther and filament
The anther is at the top — it holds pollen
The filament is the thin stalk that supports the anther
Answer: Filament

questions.q: What is the stalk that supports the stigma called?
questions.explain: The style is the tube that connects the stigma to the ovary.
procedure: The pistil has three parts: stigma, style, ovary
The stigma is at the top
The style is the middle tube that connects stigma to ovary
Answer: Style

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a way pollen can be transferred?
questions.explain: Pollen is transferred by wind, insects, birds, or water — not electricity.
procedure: Pollination happens through natural agents
Wind carries light pollen grains
Insects and birds carry pollen as they visit flowers
Water can carry pollen in some water plants
Electricity is not a pollinating agent
Answer: Electricity

questions.q: Why are petals usually brightly coloured?
options: To make the flower look nice for humans
To attract insects and birds for pollination
To protect the flower from rain
To help the flower grow taller
questions.answer: To attract insects and birds for pollination
questions.explain: Bright petals attract pollinators, which help the flower reproduce.
procedure: Many flowers need insects or birds to carry pollen
Bright colours and pleasant scents attract these pollinators
The pollinators come for nectar, but leave with pollen on their bodies
They carry the pollen to the next flower
Answer: To attract insects and birds for pollination

questions.q: Which part of the flower is usually green and found at the base?
questions.explain: The sepal is the green, leaf-like part at the base of the flower.
procedure: Look at a flower from the outside
The green, leaf-like parts at the bottom are sepals
They protect the flower bud before it opens
Answer: Sepal

questions.q: What do flowers produce that we often enjoy for their beauty and smell?
questions.explain: Flowers produce nectar and scent that attract pollinators.
procedure: Flowers make nectar (a sweet liquid) inside them
They also release scent through their petals
Both are used to attract insects and birds
Nectar also provides food for the pollinators
Answer: Nectar and scent

questions.q: A bee visits a flower and later visits another. What is the bee doing?
questions.explain: The bee carries pollen from one flower to another.
procedure: As a bee collects nectar, pollen sticks to its hairy body
When it visits the next flower, some of that pollen rubs off onto the stigma
This transfer is called pollination
The bee is helping the flowers reproduce
Answer: Pollinating the flowers

questions.q: Which part of the flower protects it while it is still a bud?
questions.explain: The sepal wraps around and protects the flower bud.
procedure: Before the flower opens, it is called a bud
The green sepals wrap around the bud
They protect the inner parts from weather and damage
Once the flower opens, the sepals are visible at the base
Answer: Sepal

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct order of the flower's life from bud to seed?
options: Bud → Flower → Pollination → Fertilization → Fruit and Seed
questions.answer: Bud → Flower → Pollination → Fertilization → Fruit and Seed
questions.explain: The flower grows from a bud, opens, gets pollinated, fertilized, and produces fruit and seeds.
procedure: 1. Bud forms (protected by sepals)
2. Bud opens into a flower with petals
3. Pollination happens (pollen reaches stigma)
4. Fertilization happens (sex cells join)
5. Ovary becomes fruit, ovules become seeds
Answer: Bud → Flower → Pollination → Fertilization → Fruit and Seed
